dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She seems to be resting. Best not to disturb her...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Did I frighten you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Arlecchino often played this game with me, but I only won once.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe I should look for her so we can play again some time.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Try sensing the power of kuuvahki, and you might spot me coming next time.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Shh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They're asleep.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You seem tired. Is this place too high up?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe installing a ladder would help...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I like being up high. I can't help but wonder... What would Teyvat look like if we looked down on it from the moon above?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: So, go to sleep, little ones, lest the fearsome whale awaken once more.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Kuuhenki are an energetic bunch. Lulling them to sleep is no easy task.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, are you here to listen to the story, too?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well, then... Take care not to be fooled by false moons.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: People often give things to the kuuhenki, praying for good luck.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'm teaching them the importance of doing things in return.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Looks like I've learned a thing or two.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I should prepare a few other pieces of music...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Would you like to sing along?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "But our main protagonist drew a topic of terrible, troubling tribulation — to find and bring back the 'undying fire.'"

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Huh... That does sound very hard. What is this "undying fire," anyway? Curious...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "'I wish to become a witch's familiar,' said the young lady."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hehe... Yes, I know. If we were in this story, I would choose you all to be my familiars, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Now then, shall I continue reading?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "It was classified as belonging to the same class and superorder as a standard demon king but was part of a different grandorder. The chipmunk demon king looked very fierce indeed."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh. You're having trouble imagining what this chipmunk demon king might look like?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should ask Maalaus to help us.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "'This is your magic teacher speaking. The trial is over. You were unable to obtain your witch license.'"

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that it? This volume seems rather short.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "Anyway, let's stop the story here..."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Don't be sad. It's just as the book says. "The little witch's adventures would continue."

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I'll read you all a new story next time. How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I'm almost done reading this "secret, unreleased" story that Miss Nicole sent us... What should I read to you all today?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I like great heights, and I also like the feeling of sitting next to you on high, just like when we were on the moon.
